findings.statement: 16 MB seals lift ingest-to-routed by at least 1.2x over 64 MB
findings.detail: 16 MB 485063 ops/s against 64 MB 495952 (16mb vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.978, p=0.8345) -- within noise, not a result); 32 MB 507443 (32mb vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.023, p=1.0000) -- within noise, not a result). Phases at 16 against 64 MB: commit 0.012s/0.011s, seal 0.013s/0.013s, merge 0.011s/0.011s; the loop alone 0.016s/0.016s. Smaller seals move the merges off the drain and onto the other cores while the load runs

findings.statement: at 16 MB seals, device bytes are at most 2.0x the 64 MB arm's
findings.detail: device bytes 9.2 MB at 16 MB seals against 9.2 at 64 MB (1.000x); 32 MB 9.2, 8 MB 9.2. Disk after the drain 3.3/3.3/3.3/3.3 MB for 64/32/16/8, partitions 1/1/1/1. Every merge round rewrites the live set the new pieces touch; this is that amplification, measured

findings.statement: reads after the drain do not differ across seal sizes
findings.detail: 123 ns per point read at 64 MB, 123 at 32, 123 at 16 (16mb vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.018, p=0.8102) -- within noise, not a result), 125 at 8 (8mb vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.037, p=1.0000) -- within noise, not a result). After the drain every arm is partitions only and the partition count is set by max_keys, not the seal size

findings.statement: the sweep has an interior optimum: 8 MB seals ingest no faster than 16 MB
findings.detail: 8 MB 478890 ops/s against 16 MB 485063 (8mb vs 16mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.987, p=0.6761) -- within noise, not a result); device bytes 9.2 against 9.2 MB, merge phase 0.011s against 0.011s. Below some size the merge amplification and the per-seal fixed costs take back what the overlap gave

findings.statement: 32 MB seals over 64 MB partitions ingest at least 1.10x the 64 MB arm
findings.detail: 32mb-p64 442270 ops/s against 64 MB 495952 (32mb-p64 vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.892, p=0.4034) -- within noise, not a result); 32 MB with coupled partitions 507443 (32mb vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.023, p=1.0000) -- within noise, not a result). Phases 32mb-p64 against 64 MB: commit 0.013s/0.011s, seal 0.014s/0.013s, merge 0.013s/0.011s; device bytes 9.2 against 9.2 MB; partitions 1 against 1. Three seals overlap the load where one did, and no extra merge round is triggered

findings.statement: 32 MB seals over 64 MB partitions read no slower than 64 MB seals after the drain
findings.detail: 120 ns per point read for 32mb-p64 against 123 at 64 MB (32mb-p64 vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.990, p=0.6889) -- within noise, not a result); 32 MB with coupled partitions 123 (32mb vs 64mb: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.017, p=1.0000) -- within noise, not a result). Same partition count, same reads; the read cost the first run charged to the seal size was the partition count's

notes: four arms interleaved in one process, fresh store per rep, one option apart: seal_bytes 64 MB (shipping), 32, 16 and 8, on f49's shape -- the f42 durable load with the drain (seal, join, partition) inside the timed window. Smaller seals move merges off the drain and onto the other cores while the load runs; the price is every merge round rewriting the live set.
